name: Retire Global ID Ordinal Probe

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Retire Global ID Ordinal Probe Hypothesis

Now that both map and vector reuse are decisively rejected, removing the temporary same-ordinal hash vectors and ninth counter will eliminate diagnostics-only per-ID vector writes, frame rotations, and propagation while preserving the durable previous-frame membership telemetry.

**Attempt Count:** 1.

### Scope Lock

Remove only experiment 107's two diagnostics-only order vectors, ninth counter, Scene/WGPU/web propagation field, and Test Suite type/assertion. Preserve all eight prior global-ID counters, product identity construction, public APIs, dependencies, and unrelated diagnostics.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Run nested formatting, diagnostics-disabled/enabled Clippy with warnings denied, focused and full gpux tests, WGPU tests, then exclusive headed Test Suite WASM/WebGPU proof at both DPRs. Require exact offsets, all retained counters, and zero errors. Compare diagnostics-build throughput and paced p95 to experiment 107 as directional evidence; the primary proof is removal of two unbounded-by-frame-capacity vector writes per creation plus their rotation state with no contract loss.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

Return global-ID diagnostics to eight durable counters, remove temporary order-vector work, and retain exact Test Suite behavior at both DPRs.

reportMarkdown:
# Retire Global ID Ordinal Probe

The completed reuse decision no longer leaves temporary order instrumentation in the diagnostics hot path. The change removes two hash vectors, one push per global-ID creation, vector rotation/clear work, the ninth scalar, and its Scene/WGPU/web/Test Suite propagation while preserving all eight durable counters and normal identity construction.

Formatting, both warnings-denied Clippy matrices, 419 gpux tests plus integrations, 52 WGPU tests, and 2/2 headed Test Suite WebGPU cases passed. Both DPRs retained the exact final offset, 485 global-ID creations, and 485 previous-frame membership hits; the retired ordinal field is absent.

Against experiment 107, throughput was effectively flat at DPR 1 (26.076848 versus 26.083318) and 4.95% higher at DPR 2 (25.280220 versus 24.088512). Paced p95 moved oppositely across DPRs, so no timing claim is made from that noise. The accepted improvement is the direct reduction in diagnostics-only work and state with unchanged retained contracts.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept removal of the temporary ordinal probe. Keep the eight durable global-ID distribution and previous-frame membership counters, and do not restore ordinal-order telemetry unless a new independent hypothesis requires it.
